findings.quote: If you get a sine or cosine of $1$ or more, you put the wrong side on top.
findings.problem: The diagnosis is false in a common case. A sine or cosine of 1 or more means the hypotenuse is not in the denominator, not that the numerator is wrong. Counterexample: a student computes sine as opposite over adjacent in a triangle where the opposite leg is longer (legs 8 and 6 give 8/6 > 1). The side on top (opposite) is correct; the wrong side is on the bottom. A student who checks the top side, as told, finds it right and cannot locate the error.
findings.source: Content checklist B01; reader rules, test every general statement; the lesson's own SOH-CAH-TOA definitions (hypotenuse in the denominator of sine and cosine)

findings.quote: Put your calculator in degree mode first. In a right triangle the other angles are acute, so the calculator's answer is the angle you want.
